newsitem.title: UK: Clarke wins standing ovation at party conference.
newsitem.headline: Clarke wins standing ovation at party conference.

text.p: UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke won a prolonged standing ovation for his speech on Thursday to the annual conference of the ruling Conservative Party.
The lengthy applause, during which Prime Minister John Major raised Clarke's hand in triumph, confounded some predictions that the finance minister would have a rough reception.
Clarke won particular cheers for his denunciation of a united states of Europe.

He spelled out the agreed government line of a wait-and-see policy on a single European currency and added: "Let us spend the next six months uniting behind that policy and attacking the Labour Party."
